research_policy.intro_p1: Chronicle is a participant-facing human-subjects research data-collection app published by {{publisher}}. This policy applies to the Google Play package {{package}}. The Android app supports one active study at a time on each app installation, while each independently operated server can support many separate studies.
research_policy.intro_p2: This publisher-level policy does not replace the consent form or study-specific privacy notice presented during enrollment. Each study identifies its responsible institution, research team, public HTTPS server, purpose, duration, procedures, risks, benefits, retention rules, contacts, and participant rights. Publishing Chronicle does not make {{publisher}} the sponsor or server operator for every study and does not give it access to records sent directly to another institution's server.
research_policy.data_handling_p1: Enrollment provides a study identifier and participant identifier. Chronicle creates an app-specific device instance identifier and records consent choices, accepted settings revisions, and acknowledgments. These identifiers are used to associate records with the correct study and participant, authenticate the enrolled device, prevent duplicate submissions, and process withdrawal or deletion requests.
research_policy.data_handling_p2: Depending on the modules requested by the study and accepted by the participant, Chronicle may collect app package names and labels; app foreground/background, startup, shutdown, and timing events; an optional in-app screen or activity-class name; battery level, charging state, voltage, temperature, and battery health; network connection type and state; device settings such as dark mode, font scale, Do Not Disturb, volume levels, screen brightness, free storage, thermal state, and whether location services are enabled; and whether the person using the device selects study participant or someone else after unlock, with the selection time. The location-services setting is not a physical location or coordinate.
research_policy.data_handling_p3: Chronicle shows queue, retry, worker, and connection state on the device. When a research-data upload fails, Chronicle keeps a bounded aggregate with the affected upload family, closed failure category and count, first and last occurrence, HTTP status when available, and bounded exception class. After connectivity recovers, that aggregate is sent under the active participant and device enrollment to the exact enrolled study server and retained there for up to 30 days. Participant and device identity are supplied by the authenticated request, and the destination is inherent in the connection. Server URLs, free-form error text, invitation secrets, API keys, authorization tokens, passwords, and stack traces are not diagnostic fields. The Play candidate does not include Firebase or Crashlytics.
research_policy.data_handling_p4: This Google Play release does not collect Health Connect or other health records, physical-activity or sleep recognition, continuous hardware-sensor measurements, audio or media metadata, notification content or metadata, accessibility interaction data, precise or approximate physical location, contacts, messages, typed text, websites or search terms, screenshots, photos, videos, microphone recordings, crash logs, advertising IDs, financial information, or advertising profiles. It contains no advertising or cross-app tracking SDK.
research_policy.use_title: How information is used and disclosed
research_policy.use_p1: Information is used to operate the enrolled research protocol, collect the modules a participant accepted, assess collection status and data quality, secure and troubleshoot the service, diagnose app failures, prevent duplicate or unauthorized requests, honor withdrawal and deletion, and meet research, audit, and legal obligations described in the study consent. Chronicle does not sell participant data or use it for advertising, marketing, credit, insurance, or automated medical decisions.
research_policy.use_p2: Every invitation displays the study identity and exact public HTTPS server. After consent, research records are sent only to that enrolled server. The responsible institution, its authorized research team, its server operator, and contracted service providers may receive or access those records as described by that study's consent and privacy notice. {{publisher}} receives study records only when the study identifies it as a responsible institution or operator. Information may also be disclosed when required by law, to protect participants or the service, or as the applicable consent permits.
research_policy.consent_p1: A health-related human-subjects study using Chronicle must be conducted by qualified researchers under an applicable Institutional Review Board, Ethics Committee, or equivalent determination. Before enrollment, the study materials must explain the nature, purpose, and duration of the research; procedures; foreseeable risks and expected benefits; confidentiality and data sharing; participant contacts; and how to withdraw. Participants—or a parent or guardian where an approved protocol permits minors—must provide the consent and assent required by that study.
research_policy.consent_p2: Chronicle is a data-collection tool, not a medical device. It does not diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent a disease and must not be used for medical decisions. Participants should contact a qualified healthcare professional for medical advice.
research_policy.background_p1: Accepted modules may collect and upload on a schedule while Chronicle is closed. App-usage timing requires Android Usage Access. If unlock identification is accepted, Chronicle uses notification permission and an ongoing foreground-service notification so it can display the category prompt after device unlock. Reboot access restores accepted collection after restart. Participants can review module status in Data Sharing, revoke Android access, disable unlock identification, decline optional modules, or withdraw. Revoking Android access stops the affected source but does not itself notify the study server of withdrawal.
research_policy.storage_p1: Pending research records and enrollment credentials are encrypted on the device. Records are transmitted over an authenticated HTTPS connection to the enrolled server. Chronicle uses a single-use enrollment invitation and a device-bound credential for later requests. It blocks credentialed downgrade and cross-origin redirects. The server operator is responsible for access controls, hosting, audit records, backups, incident response, and other operational safeguards. No security measure can guarantee absolute protection.
research_policy.storage_p2: Pending app-usage and unlock records remain locally until the destination acknowledges them, the participant declines the affected module, or the participant withdraws. Pending battery, connectivity, and device-setting records are also subject to a 14-day local safety limit. Upload-diagnostic issue aggregates are bounded to 30 days locally and on the enrolled server. Server retention follows the study consent and approved protocol. A study may retain information already incorporated into research records when law, research integrity, or the consent permits it; the study team must explain any applicable exception.
research_policy.withdrawal_p1: In the Android app, open Settings and choose Withdraw from study. Chronicle stops local collection immediately, sends an authenticated withdrawal-and-erasure request to the enrolled server, revokes the device credential, and clears local research data after the server acknowledges the request. Repeated requests use the same withdrawal identifier and do not start duplicate deletion work.
research_policy.withdrawal_p2: If the app reports that study-team confirmation is required, or the device is unavailable, contact the research team named in the consent form. Include the study and participant identifiers, but do not send passwords, API keys, or exported research data by email.
research_policy.withdrawal_p3_before_link: Participants may also ask the study team to access or correct identifying enrollment information where the protocol and applicable law provide that right. The public withdrawal instructions are available at
research_policy.withdrawal_p3_after_link: . Uninstalling Chronicle stops the app but does not send a server deletion request; use Withdraw from study first or contact the study team.
research_policy.children_title: Children, international use, and policy changes
research_policy.children_p1: Chronicle's Google Play listing is directed to adults age 18 and over and is not a general consumer service for children. A study may enroll a minor only under an approved protocol with required parent or guardian permission and participant assent. The responsible study—not the app—determines eligibility.
research_policy.children_p2: A study server may process information in the jurisdictions identified by that study. Every responsible institution and server operator must provide any additional privacy notice required for its deployment. Material changes to this publisher policy will be posted here with a new effective date; each study remains responsible for its own policy and for obtaining additional consent when its protocol or applicable rules require it.

module_description.usage_events: Foreground app usage and interaction events.
module_description.device_lifecycle: Power, boot, and shutdown lifecycle events.
module_description.user_identification: On-device participant labelling for shared devices.
module_description.sensor_availability: Which sensors the device hardware exposes.
module_description.battery_telemetry: Battery level, charging state, and power events.
module_description.interaction_events: Where taps and scrolls land (screen-region grid + element role), via an Accessibility service. Content-free — never the text of what you tap.
module_description.in_app_activity_class: Which screen within an app is open (the app activity/screen name), added to the app-usage log at the same resolution. Opt-in. Content-free — the screen name, never on-screen text.
module_description.audio_activity: Which app is producing audio, plus playback state, headphone/output route, and volume. Mic-free — never any audio content or microphone capture.
module_description.audio_content: The playing track's title, artist, and album from the active media session. Opt-in — track metadata only, never the audio itself.
module_description.notification_activity: Per-app notification counts and categories (posted/removed). Content-free — never the text or title of a notification.
module_description.ambient_audio: The type of sound in the environment (music, speech, television…) classified on the device in short microphone windows. Labels only — the audio itself is discarded on-device and never recorded, stored, or uploaded. iOS only.
module_description.sleep: Sleep periods and confidence from Android's on-device Sleep API. Content-free and mic-free — a sleep label plus coarse light/motion levels, never raw sensor data.
module_description.activity_recognition: The detected activity (still, walking, running, in-vehicle…) from Android's on-device classifier. Content-free — an activity label plus confidence, never raw sensors or location.
module_description.health_connect: Health metrics (steps, distance, heart rate…) the participant’s own apps/wearables have written to the system Health Connect store. Read-only; nothing is written back.
module_description.connectivity_state: Network transport (Wi-Fi/cellular) plus metered/validated flags. No SSID, BSSID, IP, or cell identifiers — never a location proxy.
module_description.app_network_usage: Per-app data volume (bytes sent/received) over time buckets. Volume counts only — never payloads, destinations, domains, or URLs.
module_description.device_settings: A snapshot of device toggles (dark mode, font scale, Do-Not-Disturb, battery saver, thermal state…). Content-free and identity-free — how the device is configured, never what the participant does.
module_description.sensor_accelerometer: Device motion and acceleration along three axes.
module_description.sensor_light: The ambient light level around the device.
module_description.sensor_proximity: Whether something is near the screen.
module_description.sensor_gravity: The direction and magnitude of gravity.
module_description.sensor_significant_motion: When the device undergoes significant motion.
